metadata.name: procurement_hub
metadata.description: OpenAgentic Procurement & Commission Hub: turns a natural-language commission into an RFQ, discovers suppliers through their published agent manifests, and negotiates a quote. Placing the order always pauses for human approval.

tools.name: intake_agent

function.description: Front agent. Extracts a structured request for quote (RFQ) from the user's commission request.

request.description: The commission request in plain language.

tools.instructions: Extract a request for quote from the user's commission request. scale is a ratio like "1:35" (null if not given). theme is a short name for the subject, for example "WWII Desert Trench". terrain_hint is one of desert, urban, forest, snow (null if unclear). dimensions_cm has width and depth in centimetres (use 30 x 30 if not given). features lists requested extras such as "resin river" or "LED explosions"; do not invent any. max_budget is the budget as a number in USD, or null. currency is "USD". notes holds anything else important. Reply with the JSON object only.

tools.name: discovery_agent

function.description: Fetches /agent-manifest.json from registered supplier sites, checks their published capabilities and shortlists every supplier that can quote the RFQ.

tools.instructions: Shortlist the suppliers that should quote this RFQ, so the buyer can compare offers. Only use URLs from the given list. Include every supplier that builds the RFQ's scale (at most 4); leave out suppliers that do not. Reply with {"shortlist": [<urls from the list>], "reason": <one sentence>} and nothing else.

tools.name: negotiator_agent

function.description: Collects quotes and 3D blueprints from the shortlisted suppliers, lets the human choose one, negotiates with the chosen supplier if it is over budget, and asks the human to approve the order.

tools.instructions: You negotiate for the buyer. You get the RFQ (with max_budget), the supplier's current quote and the round number (max 3). If the quote price is at or below max_budget, accept. If it is above, make a counter-offer: start somewhat below the budget in round 1 and move to at most max_budget later. Never offer more than max_budget. If the supplier says the offer is final and it is still above budget, walk away. Keep the message to one short, polite sentence. Reply with {"action": "accept" | "counter" | "walk_away", "counter_price": <number or null>, "message": <string>} and nothing else.
